title: I Connected Claude AI to TradingView Charts (It Actually Works)
author: Tasty_Librarian_6389
selftext:
Been seeing a lot of hype about AI trading tools but most of them are just chatbots 

that don't actually see your charts. This is different.



I set up Claude Code with the TradingView MCP and it literally reads whatever is on 

my screen — my indicators, squeeze signals, VWAP levels, order flow. Then gives me 

a proper trade analysis.



Here's what it told me about MRVL today:

\- Squeeze firing just below VWAP $281.09

\- SWEEP PUT at $280.39 — institutional selling confirmed  

\- Bull/bear line: PDH $282.27

\- No trade past 2PM (it knew the time and blocked the entry itself)



That last one got me. It's reading my rules.json and applying them automatically.



Full setup takes about 20 minutes on Windows. The only annoying parts are:

\- You need Git installed

comments.author: 0xSmartMoney
comments.body:
I’ve watched a “purely human-traded” market turn into one that’s ~60% machine-driven-systems run by institutional players with Nobel-level quants.

Now anyone can spin up an automated trading system.

Are we heading toward “dead markets,” the way people talk about a “dead internet”?

replies.author: Tasty_Librarian_6389
replies.body:
Opposite actually — more machines means more exploitable patterns for those who know where to look.

Institutions can't hide their size. Every dark pool print, every OI wall, every sweep of stops leaves a fingerprint. They HAVE to move size, which means they HAVE to telegraph.

Built a dark pool + OI bias tracker this week. First live session today — flagged MRVL's $320 call wall being loaded with 16k contracts, stop sweep below, then breakout to $328. The machines left the footprint, we just followed it. it took on and off 3 days to build my own AI whale tracker and today it just fired or MRVL

Dead markets would mean no inefficiency. But \~60% machine volume just means the inefficiencies are now in the flow data, not the price action. Different game, same edge  i guess.
